newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: UN court to rule on jurisdiction in US-Iran case.
newsitem.headline: UN court to rule on jurisdiction in US-Iran case.

text.p: The International Court of Justice said on Monday it would decide on Thursday whether it had jurisdiction in a dispute over the destruction of three Iranian oil platforms by U.S. warships almost 10 years ago.
Iran has asked the U.N. court to rule that the attacks on the oil platforms in October 1987 and April 1988 violated international law and that the U.S. should pay damages.
But Washington has urged the judges to throw the case out, arguing that the strikes were a legitimate response to attacks on a U.S. frigate and an oil tanker sailing under the U.S. flag.
The disputed events date back to the final stages of the 1980-88 war between Iran and Iraq when the U.S. sent naval forces to the Gulf to protect international shipping.
Tehran took the case to the Hague-based court in 1992, arguing that its 1955 Treaty of Amity with Washington provided a legal basis for the U.N. court to settle the dispute.
But at hearings in September, the United States argued that the Treaty of Amity governed commercial and consular affairs and that political and military matters fell outside its scope.
The court will rule on Thursday whether the treaty provides a sufficient basis for its jurisdiction over the case.

If the court rules that it does not have jurisdiction, then the case will go no further. But if it decides it does have jurisdiction, then the court will hold further proceedings to examine the underlying issues at the heart of the dispute.
